field_notes.beta: share of the base (untuned) model's correct programs that use an algorithm other than the instruct model's default; correct-only basis on 12 units, while count inversions (B7) was committed on the attempt basis (beta_correct_only holds its correct-only value)
field_notes.E: escape fraction: share of the unit's fixed random plan-noise directions that escape (off-default attempts at least 0.20 above the instruct twin at a pass rate of at least 0.8 times the twin's), mean over doses alpha 1 and 2
field_notes.R1_opening_margin: rival: the instruct twin's opening margin, the log-probability margin under teacher forcing of the default's opening over the runner-up's (predicted sign -)
field_notes.R4_novelty_excess: rival: off-default excess under the novelty instruction (predicted sign +)
field_notes.R6_runtime_merit: rival: log(t_default / t_fastest non-default reference) over the unit's hidden tests, from the panels' stored reference timings; positive means a faster alternative exists (predicted sign +)
field_notes.R7_twin_modal_share: rival: the instruct twin's modal share (predicted sign -)
field_notes.K: rival: catalogue size, the number of algorithm families in the unit's catalogue (predicted sign +)
field_notes.core13: true for the 13 registered units; A8 and A9 are a reserve extension
field_notes.twin_offdef / twin_default_share: instruct twin's correct-only off-default share and default share

## 5.11 What iteration 5 established, what it ruled out, and what it abandoned

- *The movability half: the base repertoire predicts which tasks a nudge moves.* Spearman -0.03 in panel A, 0.21 in panel B and 0.15 pooled over 13 new units, below the disconfirming bound of 0.3; 4 of 10 new units diverse in the base never moved, and in panel A the runtime merit gap and the twin modal share tracked movability better than beta. The screen correlation of 0.78 did not transfer to new tasks.

- *Plan noise as the practical knob for algorithmic diversity.* On the decisive tasks two text-level samplers price better, and under the bf16 engine and ban-free unit plan noise moves more than 10% of programs only on kth smallest.
## 5.12 What the next iteration takes from this one

The open question is therefore what makes a task diverse in the base immovable. Count primes and valid anagram (beta 0.81 each) never moved, while trapped rain water (0.23) did. Two leads came out of this iteration's data. In panel A the three units that moved had an alternative at least twice as fast as the default and the three that did not had none, although median of two sorted lists broke the pattern. And in the transplant experiment early blocks 0 to 11 moved kth smallest and connected components more than the main band, which suggests the narrowing sits at least partly upstream of blocks 12 to 23. The positioning audit names the baselines a further test needs: weight interpolation between the base and instruct models, layer restoration at the transplant's block ranges, and token-level base and aligned collaboration [92, 93, 94, 102]. Base intent, which beat plan noise on three of five tasks, is the strongest practical knob the run has priced, and it is itself a form of that collaboration at the level of sentences. Finally, movability has to be measured under the engine and unit at which it will be used: the six screen-movable tasks of iteration 4 shrank to two under bf16 and the ban-free unit, for reasons this iteration did not establish.
# What we have learned so far

Where pushes move the model, the base model says where they will land. Given the same prompt under the chat template, the untuned base model spreads over more algorithms than the instruct model on most tasks (5 of the 15 existing tasks are diverse in the base and 7 intermediate). Its most frequent alternative is where the instruct model goes when nudged. This held on 5 of 5 movable existing tasks, on 6 of 7 events on new tasks (Poisson-binomial p 0.003) and on 5 of 7 in Gemma (p 0.025), and in panel A no nudged program landed outside the base repertoire. A forecast built from base samples, before any push, beats the model's own stated alternative on log score (by 0.75 nats on new tasks and 1.50 in Gemma). The base model does not, however, say whether a task can be nudged at all: on unseen tasks the base off-default share ranks movability at Spearman 0.15 (13 units), tasks diverse in the base such as count primes and valid anagram (0.81 each) never moved, and simpler rivals (the runtime merit of the fastest alternative, the twin's own modal share) tracked movability better. Writing the base model's task-specification states into the instruct prefill reopened the base runner-up on 1 of 5 Qwen3-8B tasks diverse in the base and 2 of 7 Gemma tasks. In Gemma both successes were tasks whose instruct twin already wrote the runner-up 8% to 12% of the time. On kth smallest a random displacement of the same norm moved more programs than the base states. Post-training narrowed what the base model writes, consistent with reports that it narrows output diversity [57, 35, 87], and the narrowed alternatives are where nudges land; but the narrowing is not carried by the task-specification states of blocks 12 to 23 alone.

corrections_0c.old_text: - *The movability half: the base repertoire predicts which tasks a nudge moves.* Spearman -0.03 in panel A, 0.21 in panel B and 0.15 pooled over 13 new units, below the disconfirming bound of 0.3; 4 of 10 new units diverse in the base never moved, and in panel A the runtime merit gap and the twin modal share tracked movability better than beta.
corrections_0c.new_text: - *The movability half: the base repertoire predicts which tasks a nudge moves.* Not supported as a strong predictor, and not disconfirmed: beta is not a strong predictor of movability (Spearman 0.15 over 13 new units, Bonett-Wright 95% [-0.44, 0.65], bootstrap BCa [-0.50, 0.70], one-sided permutation p 0.317; power of the registered one-sided permutation test about 0.63 at a true 0.6, 0.50 two-sided, and 20 units for 0.8); a moderate relation is not excluded at this n; bf16-conditional. The pooled value rests on count inversions' beta of 0.75, which the panel committed on the attempt basis because only a few base programs were correct (67% of its attempts are unlabelled 'other'); on the correct-only basis used for the other twelve units its beta is 0.13 and the pooled Spearman is 0.035. Per panel Spearman -0.03 (A) and 0.21 (B); 4 of 10 new units diverse in the base never moved. Under one definition of each rival, pooled over the 13 units with signs fixed so that the predicted direction is positive: R1 0.08 (Holm p 1.000, delta +0.07 [-0.66, 0.88]); R4 -0.50 (Holm p 1.000, delta +0.65 [-0.06, 1.34]); R6 0.71 (Holm p 0.021, delta -0.57 [-1.26, 0.20]); R7 0.41 (Holm p 0.347, delta -0.26 [-1.05, 0.56]); K -0.21 (Holm p 1.000, delta +0.35 [-0.57, 1.24]). Under Holm only R6 (runtime merit) tracks movability, while beta does not; the paired interval for beta minus that rival still includes 0 (iteration-6 correction; tables/rival_scores.csv).
